content:
This looks quite interesting. ChatGPT's latest update has added a new Mac integration feature: it can handle conversations in Apple's "Messages" app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now has an Apple Messages plugin added

The new Apple Messages plugin allows ChatGPT to read and search chat history on Mac, as well as prepare and send messages. OpenAI stated that this feature is available to all plans of the macOS version of the ChatGPT desktop app, with support for both ChatGPT Work and Codex.

This kind of access raises concerns about privacy and control, so OpenAI emphasises that sending messages still requires user approval under default settings. Users should think carefully before granting permanent approval. OpenAI's plugin guidelines detail the related risks, how to revoke access, and a known issue involving tasks that bypass approval prompts.

For now, this feature only works on Macs with Apple Silicon chips and does not support Intel models.

If you really ask ChatGPT to send a message on your behalf, it will pop up a confirmation prompt before sending. You can choose to skip this confirmation step in individual conversations.

Looking for this new feature in ChatGPT? This link takes you directly to the Messages plugin for ChatGPT on Mac.

New features like shared website co-editing and conversation snapshot sharing

Although the Messages plugin is the most eye-catching new feature for Apple users, this update also brings several other improvements. For example, pinned conversations can now be synced between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, so users can revisit important conversations at any time between Mac and iPhone.

ChatGPT also now allows users to share read-only snapshots of local Codex conversations. These snapshots do not change when the original conversation is updated.

Links created from personal accounts can be opened by anyone who has the URL, while links for workspaces are limited to members of that workspace only. OpenAI says Codex will mask known sensitive formats, but reminds users to check snapshot content as sensitive data may still remain.

Additionally, website owners can invite active members of the same workspace to co-edit collaboratively supported sites. Editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish changes after the owner completes the initial publication. Owners still retain control over access, settings, analytics, and version restoration.

Some website owners can also change the URL hosted by ChatGPT without redeploying, with old URLs automatically redirecting to the new ones.

Finally, the "Computer History" feature launched last week will be expanded to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK. This opt-in feature requires "Memories" to be enabled and is off by default.

You can see the full release announcement for this update here.
